description: The Vermont Wastewater Infrastructure Map publishes statewide GeoJSON layers for sewer and stormwater lines, point assets, service areas, treatment facilities and municipal boundaries. University of Vermont students assembled the resource with the Vermont Agency of Natural Resources from municipal and state records. The data page lists six files, including 196,169 linear features, 185,223 point features and 186 sewer-service boundaries. Geographic coverage is Vermont's 256 municipalities; most collection work ran from 2024 to June 2025, while individual source dates vary and the published layers are a snapshot, not a live sensor feed. Files are freely accessible from the project data page and repository. The README describes the dataset as public-domain; the GitHub MIT licence applies to the code and the individual source layers should be checked for downstream republication. A limitation is that source dates and ownership fields are inconsistent or missing in places, and proposed assets are mixed with existing assets under a status field. The layers support sewer-network, stormwater capacity and flood-exposure simulations. The catalogue's model-epanet is a separate hydraulic solver that could use cleaned network geometry, but no conversion was tested. No GeoJSON file was downloaded.
